takeaway: Osmolality changes are detected in the hypothalamus; ADH, made there and released from the posterior pituitary, makes the collecting duct more permeable to water.

question.text: Which of the following statements relating to antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is true?
question.say: Which of the following statements relating to anti-diuretic hormone, A D H, is true?

answer.text: Changes in osmolality are detected in the hypothalamus.
answer.say: Changes in osmolality are detected in the hypothalamus.

lines.text: Follow the story from the left. Salty blood means high osmolality.
The watchtower in the hypothalamus is the sensor: it detects changes in osmolality.
That is the true statement, and it is our answer.
The hypothalamus makes ADH, and the posterior pituitary releases it.
ADH makes aquaporins fuse with the membrane of the collecting duct cells.
The duct becomes more permeable to water, so more water is absorbed, and less urine is passed.
Low blood volume, sensed by stretch receptors in the left atrium, raises ADH rather than lowering it.
lines.say: (clears throat) Low blood volume, sensed by stretch receptors in the left atrium, raises ADH rather than lowering it.
